fix(cpp): make the C++ gateway branch build and pass its full suite again after the JSON and encoding library changes

CONTEXT (you have no other context than this prompt and the repository)
You start from branch `agent-jobs/cppgw-ci-workflow-20261118-44205765037-1` (the port branch `claude/cpp-gateway-port` plus a repaired CI workflow, pull request https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/pull/1371). `cpp/gateway/` is a C++20 port of this repository's TypeScript gateway with 441 test binaries (`cpp/gateway/tests/**/*_test.cpp`). Every deployment target is 64-bit ARM. Read `cpp/gateway/docs/CI.md` (the portable driver `cpp/gateway/tools/ci-build.sh`), `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-ci-workflow-20261118.md` (the previous agent's exact failure table, your starting evidence), `cpp/gateway/docs/DEVIATIONS-FROM-BUN.md` and `cpp/gateway/docs/OSS-REPLACEMENT-PLAN.md`.

HOW THE BRANCH GOT HERE
The last known-good state was commit 55afcc8b1 (441 of 441 binaries, 5,024 cases, hand-written JSON parser still present as a fallback behind simdjson). After it, work in progress was committed mid-change: the hand-written JSON parser was deleted so that simdjson 5.2.0 is the only parser (746 lines removed, error text is now the generic `Invalid JSON`), UTF conversion moved to simdutf, input limits were added (`include/uos/rt/limits.hpp`), and a base64/hex replacement was started but not finished.

OWNER POLICY (binding): standard library behaviour is the reference; exact parity with Bun's quirks and error-message wording is NOT required; less first-party code is preferred. What must still hold: the gateway's functional behaviour (wire formats, status codes, stored data, authentication and validation decisions, accounting) and security never getting weaker.

CURRENT STATE (observed on x64 Ubuntu 26.04, Clang 21, by the previous agent)
1. The tree does not compile: `cpp/gateway/src/rt/crypto.cpp:839:14: error: use of undeclared identifier 'HEX'` in `randomUUID()`: the lowercase hex alphabet was removed together with the old `toHex`. Every test links every runtime object, so nothing links.
2. With that constant supplied by a compiler flag, all 441 binaries link and 424 pass. Two failures are the documented ARM64-only fixtures on x64 (`permissions_linux_test`, `runtime_native_startup_test`); ignore them on x64, they must pass on ARM64. The other 15 are real and fall into classes:
   a. Tests that assert Bun's detailed parser messages where the code now reports `Invalid JSON` (for example `deepseek_stream_differential_test`, `claude_code_models_differential_test`, `native_addon_differential_test`, `kv_conversion_legacy_codec_differential_test`, `anthropic_chat_stream_differential_test`, `passkeys_webauthn_differential_test`). Under the policy these expectations change to the new message; record the class once in `DEVIATIONS-FROM-BUN.md`.
   b. Binaries that now die with `terminate called after throwing an instance of 'uos::rt::SyntaxError' what(): Invalid JSON` (signal 11): `compaction_summary_forwarding_test`, `native_authority_test`, `native_principal_control_test`, `native_runtime_binding_test`; and `jev_compaction_differential_test` with `uncaught exception: Invalid JSON`. These need diagnosis, not expectation edits: find the input that the old parser accepted and simdjson rejects (or an error that used to be caught and now escapes), and decide: if real clients or stored data can produce that input, the gateway must keep accepting it (smallest adapter, or fix the call site); if the test only fed deliberately malformed JSON, restore the proper error handling so the exception is caught where it used to be.
   c. Behaviour changes that look functional: `kernel_attestation_differential_test` now fails with `failed to parse kernel attestation JWT parts: Invalid JSON` where the expected outcome was the specific `'alg' MUST be 'RS256', got 'null'` rejection (an authentication path: the decision must still be a rejection, and valid tokens must still verify; check that the JWT header/payload reach the parser intact, e.g. padding/length handling required by simdjson); `harmony_differential_test` `normalizeToolArguments` returns `"1e400"` where `"null"` was expected (number out of double range: decide what a client-visible tool-argument normaliser should do and keep it consistent); `native_codex_429_differential_test` digest `b73ef4a13b381702` expected, `16605f5f878cd9e7` observed (find which serialised bytes changed and whether any consumer depends on them); `anthropic_replay_test` line 483 "restored payloads carry Bun's canonical key order" (object key order after parse/stringify: integer-like keys are no longer reordered; if nothing functional depends on the order, change the expectation and record it).

TASK
1. Finish the base64/hex step: `randomUUID()` and any other user of the removed alphabet must compile; use the vendored simdutf (`cpp/gateway/third_party/simdutf`) or a trivial local table, whichever is less code. Check the rest of `crypto.cpp`/`base64.cpp` for other half-finished edits.
2. Work through classes a, b and c above, one commit per class or per test, applying the policy. For every expectation you change, be able to say why it is a wording/quirk difference and not a functional one; for every functional difference, fix the code.
3. Run the whole suite with the driver until it is green: `CXX=clang++ UOS_CI_JOBS=4 bash cpp/gateway/tools/ci-build.sh --config release --shard N/4` for N = 1..4, and once with `--config asan` for the tests you touched.
4. Report: `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-suite-repair-20261118.md`: per failing test, root cause, fix or expectation change with justification, final counts per shard.

YOUR MACHINE: GitHub-hosted Linux ARM64 runner (Ubuntu 24.04, 4 CPUs, 16 GB, sudo, network). Its packages are too old for this tree: install Clang 21 or newer from apt.llvm.org, build Boost 1.92.0 `json` and `container` from the official source archive under a temp directory (the tree needs Boost >= 1.86), install OpenSSL 3, zlib, ICU, brotli, zstd development packages and build SQLite 3.54.0 exactly as `.github/workflows/cpp-gateway-ci.yml` does. Bun 1.4.0 can be installed if you need to see what the TypeScript does. After your branch is pushed the CI workflow runs the four ARM64 shards on it automatically; the maintainer reads that run as the acceptance evidence.

OWNED PATHS: anything under `cpp/gateway/` that this repair needs (sources, tests, docs). Do not edit `.github/`, the TypeScript, `cpp/gateway/third_party/` (vendored code stays unmodified) or `cpp/` outside `cpp/gateway/`. Do not delete tests. Do not start new library replacements: other agents are doing URL, HTTP parsing, regex, WebSocket, CBOR, ASN.1, BigInt and Unicode on their own branches; keep your diff minimal in those files (`src/rt/url.cpp`, `regex*.cpp`, `websocket*.cpp`, `number.cpp`, `string.cpp`, `src/runtime/http.cpp`, `src/rt/fetch_transport_http.cpp`, `src/auth/passkeys.cpp`) so the branches merge.

RULES
- The runner holds a model gateway token: never print it or write any credential to a file. Run tests with an empty `HOME`, a fresh `TMPDIR` and no provider variables (the driver does this).
- Commit small steps often; keep the report current from the start. Leave no build output in the checkout.

DONE WHEN
All four `--config release` shards pass on your ARM64 runner with zero failing binaries, the report lists every one of the 15 tests with its resolution, and `git status` is clean.
